rows.title: The hunt is on for Colorado’s next gold rush: Geological hydrogen
rows.standfirst: With scientists rethinking approach, the Front Range is quickly becoming a hub in the search underground for hydrogen

rows.title: New Denver coffee shop is serving up hand-crafted lattes and jobs for homeless teens
rows.standfirst: Purple Door, which opened near downtown in March, hires baristas who’ve gone through a job readiness program at an Englewood coffee roaster

rows.title: If downtown Denver building owners convert empty offices to residential, will people move in?
rows.standfirst: The city of Denver is all in for converting underutilized offices into apartments. There’s also a proposal to provide $5 million at the state level. But high costs and ill-suited buildings could foil plans.

rows.title: Denver is closing all migrant hotel shelters but one, a signal that services are winding down
rows.standfirst: The city had planned to keep three hotel shelters open for migrants but announced Monday that it would consolidate services at one hotel

rows.title: Colorado business leaders are neutral about the economy — the best they’ve felt in two years
rows.standfirst: The latest CU business survey has local business leaders feeling better about their profits and sales than in mid-2022. But slowing job growth and the election kept their outlook uncertain.

rows.title: Denver nonprofit Urban Peak embroiled in wage dispute as it completes four-story youth homeless shelter
rows.standfirst: Emails about the construction project reveal confusion and miscommunication between city departments about wage requirements

rows.title: Denver to Istanbul flights on Turkish Airlines begin June 11. More international routes are in the hopper.
rows.standfirst: At 6,130 miles, the flight will be the longest to and from the Mile High City

rows.title: A new plan for the Stanley Hotel in Estes Park: Sell it to Colorado bonding authority
rows.standfirst: After a deal to sell the Stanley Hotel to a nonprofit crumbled, the Colorado Educational and Cultural Facilities Authority plans to buy the historic property

rows.title: Colorado is working on alternatives to a discount internet program ending in May
rows.standfirst: Affordable Connectivity Program participants were notified this month that it is ending. Congress is mulling a $7 billion extension to keep ACP operating till the end of 2024.

rows.title: What’s Working: Stolen AT&T customer data was years old. Is it too late to protect your data?
rows.standfirst: AT&T’s recent discovery of data linked to 73 million users was more than 4 years old. Colorado security experts weigh in on how to keep data safer.

rows.title: How Colorado’s “for-cause eviction” law will affect renters and landlords
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1098 was approved by the House in February and then by the Senate at the end of March. Gov. Jared Polis signed it on April 19.

rows.title: Agencies downgrade Tri-State bonds, adding to rural power cooperative’s ongoing pressures
rows.standfirst: The move follows the announced departures of four member co-ops that cut ties seeking cleaner electricity and cheaper rates

rows.title: Boulder County: Xcel gave inadequate notice before outages left 55,000 without power
rows.standfirst: The power company stands by its handling of the pre-planned outage after weekend shut-off had residents and disaster agencies scrambling

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers approve bill to require landlords to complete serious repairs faster
rows.standfirst: A basic housing standards law has been in place since 2008, but legislators and advocates have long sought improvements

rows.title: Pagosa Springs has a housing crisis. Somehow, CHiPs star Erik Estrada is part of the answer.
rows.standfirst: The CHiPs star once marketed real estate for a shifty investment company from California. Now, Archuleta County is using the repossessed lots for critical workforce housing.

rows.title: Denver restores public services, creates asylum-seeker job program as part of expected $90 million in migrant aid
rows.standfirst: The $90 million in estimated spending on migrant services in 2024 is about half as much as was predicted back in January

rows.title: Denver inflation drops to 2.8%, opposite the national trend of rising prices
rows.standfirst: The Denver region typically has higher inflation than the rest of the nation. Prices still rose, but lower gasoline costs in March are credited for the slowdown.

rows.title: What’s Working: Denver-based Guild’s CEO talks about AI, frontline workers and her new job
rows.standfirst: The Denver tech company helps workers get ahead with education, even as AI disrupts jobs. Plus: Ibotta preps for public stock debut, Denver’s lower inflation rate and more!

rows.title: State lawmakers take steps to limit HOA foreclosures, equity loss after Colorado Sun investigation
rows.standfirst: Two measures advancing through the Colorado legislature would limit attorneys fees in HOA foreclosure cases and set a minimum bid for HOA-foreclosed homes that are being auctioned off

rows.title: Thousands of affordable housing units are at risk in Colorado. A bill would help local governments buy them.
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1175 would give local governments a “right of first refusal” to buy privately owned affordable housing once its rent restrictions expire.

rows.title: Plan to quadruple property taxes on short-term rentals in Colorado fails in late-night Capitol committee vote
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 33 was voted down 6-1 in the Senate Finance Committee during its first hearing and after months of loud opposition from vacation rental owners and companies like Airbnb and Vrbo

rows.title: Colorado’s startup community rallies behind Ibotta as Denver’s popular consumer app has IPO
rows.standfirst: Rare are startups that go from idea to a publicly traded company. Rarer still are when they’re homegrown in Colorado.

rows.title: Preemptive power outage caused chaos in Boulder County during wind storm, Xcel customers testify
rows.standfirst: Testimony to Colorado Public Utilities Commission points to lack of communication by Xcel in the hours before powerlines were powered down as a hedge against wildfire

rows.title: Denver-based Ibotta opens public trading at $107 per share
rows.standfirst: The retail-tech company’s first day of public trading hit a high of $117 per share before leveling off around $100 in mid-morning trades. Ibotta plans to invest in its cash-back and shopping technology for consumers and big retailers.

rows.title: Meow Wolf lays off 50 Denver employees during companywide reorganization
rows.standfirst: The immersive arts group, which opened its Denver location in 2021, laid off 159 employees in four states

rows.title: Eldora ski area claims “improper conduct” tainted patrollers’ vote to unionize
rows.standfirst: 76% of paid patrollers turned out for the election. Eldora management says more volunteer patrollers’ votes should have been considered.

rows.title: What’s Working: More than 50% of Colorado’s businesses employ workers outside the state
rows.standfirst: More companies added insurance policies to cover multiple states, workers’ comp data shows. Plus: Colorado unemployment rate increases to 3.7%, DEN grows and more!

rows.title: Boulder County’s Sans Souci mobile home park jumped at Colorado’s “opportunity to purchase.” Here’s how it’s going.
rows.standfirst: Nearly three years ago, Sans Souci mobile home park became a resident-owned community with the help of a new Colorado law. Now it’s facing some challenges.

rows.title: A unique Denver coffee shop has lost half its business due to nearby construction. It’s pleading for community help.
rows.standfirst: Prodigy Coffeehouse, which trains young adults through an apprenticeship program, has struggled to retain customers through heavy construction

rows.title: Xcel’s plan for new EV chargers, rebates cut by 40% by Colorado regulators
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s PUC was unconvinced Xcel’s plan was cost effective and would lead to greater adoption of electric vehicles.

rows.title: Democrats are set to unveil their Colorado property tax relief plan this week. Here’s what’s in it.
rows.standfirst: The bill aims for a long-term way to limit future spikes in businesses’ and homeowners’ tax bills with an eye toward providing more relief to people who own lower-value homes

rows.title: Alterra CEO says skiing has reached a “tipping point,” resorts need to ease pain of “really, really mad” customers
rows.standfirst: In a Q&A, we talk with Jared Smith about climate change, next-gen finance and growing skiing without tarnishing the experience

rows.title: Colorado bill to regulate generative artificial intelligence clears its first hurdle at the Capitol
rows.standfirst: Opponents of Senate Bill 205 say consumer-protection rules could stifle innovations in AI, but supporters say we need to start somewhere. The proposal is similar to another in Connecticut.

rows.title: Colorado won’t legalize raw milk this year after proposal to allow direct sales to consumers spoils in the legislature
rows.standfirst: Colorado has some of the strictest raw milk laws in the West, requiring people to buy shares in a cow or goat herd if they want to get unpasteurized milk

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers back off threat to withhold road money from cities under plan to boost housing near transit
rows.standfirst: Local government leaders across the Denver metro area remain divided over the legislation, the centerpiece of Gov. Jared Polis’ plans to reduce housing costs in Colorado

rows.title: Does Colorado help ranchers protect against wolves?
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers created a compensation fund offering up to $15,000 once Wildlife officials confirm wolves have killed livestock or working animals.

rows.title: Colorado legislature’s property tax plan is in 11th-hour limbo after state commission balks at draft proposal
rows.standfirst: The Colorado General Assembly’s 2024 legislative session ends May 8. The latest a bill could be introduced and still have enough time to pass would be May 6, a week from Monday.

rows.title: Food is money for Colorado farmers and ranchers. Here’s how the ag census report says they’re doing.
rows.standfirst: The 2022 Census of Agriculture is a valuable resource. Plus: Canceled flights and airline refunds, LGBTQ+ friendly job fair and more!

rows.title: Durango’s hotel-to-housing project financing is a first in Colorado
rows.standfirst: The Residences at Durango will provide 120 below-market rentals for people earning no more than 60% of the city’s $76,177 median household income

rows.title: U.S. 50 bridge closure is an “immediate 911 deal” for Gunnison Valley Hospital
rows.standfirst: When the Blue Mesa bridge shut down, the hospital shifted into disaster management mode, figuring out how to deliver critical care to cancer and kidney patients and how to re-route staffers and basic supplies that come over from Montrose

rows.title: Colorado’s two largest energy co-ops break from Xcel, Tri-State aiming for more local control and lower costs
rows.standfirst: Sedalia’s CORE and Brighton’s United Power say they have enough market power to strike out on their own

rows.title: Colorado Democrats announce major deal with governor to cut income taxes, redirect TABOR refunds to low-income families
rows.standfirst: The income tax rate is expected to drop for 2024 to 4.25% from 4.4%. The state sales tax rate will drop, too.
